channel.title: Evidence-Centered Design :: CS Two Year Refactor
channel.description: Working draft for faculty review. This page describes the general research basis for designing assessment around explicit evidentiary reasoning. For where this is operationalized in the program, see Chapter 5 — particularly The Competency Model, which already states the core ECD commitment: competencies belong to the program, and courses are evidence-generating contexts. What evidence-centered design is Evidence-centered design (ECD) reframes assessment design as building an explicit evidentiary argument, not writing a set of test items (Mislevy et al., 2003). The claim you want to make about a student — “this student can reason about concurrency,” “this student can design a normalized schema” — is not directly observable. An assessment is only useful to the extent that a specific, designed-in-advance chain of reasoning connects something you can observe (a work product, a performance, an answer) back to that unobservable claim. ECD’s core discipline is to design that chain deliberately, before writing a single task, rather than writing tasks first and hoping they happen to support the claims you later want to make.
